'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Qamishli clashes (2021)]]
***The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]] reports clashes from yesterday evening until this morning, resulting in the deaths of an [[Asayish (Rojava regions)|Asayish]] commander and five [[National Defence Forces|NDF]] [[militia]]men in the city of [[Qamishli]], [[al-Hasakah Governorate|al-Hasakah]]. Fighting has ceased while [[government of Russia|Russian]] mediation is ongoing. [https://www.startribune.com/clashes-between-kurdish-government-forces-kill-1-in-syria/600048404/ (''Star Tribune'')]
**[[Iran–Israel conflict during the Syrian civil war]]
***[[Israeli Air Force]] [[warplane]]s launch [[airstrike]]s against [[Syria]] after a [[S-200 (missile)|S-200]] missile landed {{convert|30|km|mi}} away from the [[Shimon Peres Negev Nuclear Research Center]] in [[Southern District (Israel)|Southern Israel]]. The [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] says the missile was launched from [[southern Syria]]. Residents in both central Israel and the [[West Bank]] report loud explosions. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/alarms-sound-in-south-of-israel-665953 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Afghan peace process]]
***[[Germany]] announces that it will withdraw its [[Bundeswehr|troops]] from [[Afghanistan]] by early July. [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/germany-plans-to-pull-troops-out-of-afghanistan-from-july-4/articleshow/82178509.cms?from=mdr (''The Economic Times'')]
*[[2021 Northern Chad offensive|Northern Chad offensive]]
**Rebels of the [[Front for Change and Concord in Chad]] (FACT) threaten to press on and reach [[Chad]]'s capital [[N'Djamena]] following the killing of President [[Idriss Déby]]. In the capital, many civilians choose to stay home as fears grow. FACT rebels reject the [[Transitional Military Council (Chad)|military junta]] led by Déby's son, [[Mahamat Déby Itno]], and opposition politicians also call for a civilian transition. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/rebels-threaten-march-capital-chad-reels-presidents-battlefield-death-2021-04-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Quetta Serena Hotel bombing]]
**A [[car bomb]] is [[detonate]]d in a hotel parking lot in [[Quetta]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], killing four people and injuring eleven others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/21/bombing-in-hotel-kills-at-least-3-in-pakistan (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**At least four [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed in an [[ambush]] in the [[Sanmatenga Province]] of [[Burkina Faso]]. [https://www.news24.com/news24/africa/news/ambush-in-burkina-faso-kills-4-soldiers-security-sources-20210421 (''News24'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*The [[Government of Indonesia|Indonesian government]] reports the disappearance of the [[submarine]] {{ship|KRI|Nanggala|402|6}} during a [[torpedo]] [[live fire exercise]], requesting [[search and rescue]] assistance from [[Singapore]] and [[Australia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesian-navy-checking-submarine-after-failure-report-back-exercise-2021-04-21/ (Reuters)]

***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****The [[Government of France|French government]] announces that the [[France|country]] will lift its domestic [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic|travel restrictions]] and ease a nationwide curfew in May amidst an expectation that the number of COVID-19 cases will be reduced. The government also announces that they will impose a 10-day quarantine on all travelers from India in order to prevent the spread of the Lineage B.1.617 variant. '''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–United States relations]]
**[[U.S. Ambassador to Belarus]] [[Julie D. Fisher]] visits [[Belarus]] opposition leader [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] on the eve of a meeting between [[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] and [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-04-21/us-ambassador-visits-belarus-opposition-leader-on-eve-of-putin-lukashenko-meeting?context=amp (U.S. News & World Report)]
*[[Afghanistan–United States relations]]
**[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] says that the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] is working with [[United States Congress|Congress]] to provide [[United States dollar|$]]300 million in aid to [[Afghanistan]] in 2021 amid fears of a  collapse of the Afghan government following the [[2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan|withdrawal]] of [[United States Armed Forces|US troops]] in September. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/joewalsh/2021/04/21/us-promises-300-million-boost-in-aid-to-afghanistan-heres-why/ (''Forbes'')]
*[[Russia–Ukraine relations]], [[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbas]]
**[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelensky]] invites his [[President of Russia|Russian counterpart]] [[Vladimir Putin]] to a face-to-face meeting on the [[front line]] in the war-torn [[Donbas]] to negotiate an end to the conflict. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/ukraines-zelenskiy-invites-putin-to-meet-on-front-line (''Daily Sabah'')]
*[[Czech Republic–Russia relations]]
**[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Czech Republic)|Czech foreign minister]] Jakub Kulhánek issues Russia with an [[ultimatum]] to return all of the Czech [[diplomat]]s it had expelled from the Czech [[embassy]] in [[Moscow]], following a series of [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocal moves]] between the two countries since April 17 to expel each other's diplomats after the [[Czechs]] discovered [[GRU (G.U.)|Russian intelligence]] involvement in the [[2014 Vrbětice ammunition warehouses explosions]]. Kulhánek threatens to expel more diplomats from the [[Embassy of Russia in Prague|Russian embassy]] in [[Prague]] if the ultimatum is not met. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/04/21/prague-gives-moscow-ultimatum-to-let-czech-diplomats-return-a73692 (''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**[[2020–2021 Minneapolis–Saint Paul racial unrest|2020–2021 Minneapolis–Saint Paul racial justice protests]], [[George Floyd protests in Minneapolis–Saint Paul]]
***[[United States Attorney General|U.S. Attorney General]] [[Merrick Garland]] announces that the [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]] will investigate whether the [[Minneapolis Police Department]] engaged in a "pattern or practice of unconstitutional, unlawful policing". [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/ag-garland-announce-federal-probe-policing-practices-minneapolis/story?id=77213763 (ABC News)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[Bundestag]] votes 342–250 to approve the proposed Infection Protection Act that will give [[Fourth Merkel cabinet|Angela Merkel's government]] to impose uniform restrictions in areas where infection rate is very high. 152 people are arrested in [[Protests over COVID-19 policies in Germany|demonstrations]] against the controversial law. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/04/21/thousands-protest-in-berlin-as-parliament-votes-on-new-covid-restrictions (Euronews)] [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-04-21/protesters-gather-as-germany-debates-covid-19-lockdown-law?fbclid=IwAR065CdkTMukRb_IIOZsWESwfbxydtyyj5D1n08dV9PPjC6VmPXuNgogo64 (U.S. News & World Report)]
*[[Domestic violence in Australia]]
**A nine-month-old girl is [[murder]]ed by her father at the [[Whispering Wall]] in [[South Australia]]. The perpetrator, already known by police for incidents involving domestic violence, commits [[suicide]] at the scene. [https://www.news.com.au/national/south-australia/henry-kobi-shepherdson-identified-as-victims-of-whispering-wall-murdersuicide/news-story/5aa8cee5a3e6cd3d0414a75044ad1fca (News.com.au)]
*The [[Government of Sri Lanka|Sri Lankan government]] expels an [[Antigua and Barbuda|Antigua]]-registered [[cargo ship]] docked at the [[Magampura Mahinda Rajapaksa Port]] after authorities discovered undeclared [[uranium hexafluoride]] bound for [[China]]. The government pledges to take legal action against the ship's owner. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210421-sri-lanka-expels-ship-carrying-nuclear-material-for-china (France 24)]
